title: A complete read-model run
statement: Let $c$ be a configuration with $m$ registers, let $r\ne s$ be register indices, and let $i$ be a natural number. Suppose register $r$ contains the binary word for $i$ and its head is at position $0$. Starting with register $s$ loaded with the binary word for $0$, its head at $0$, the input head at position $1$, and the state at the initial read phase, the read model reaches a configuration with register $s$ containing the symbol of the input at index $i$ (or blank if that index is out of range), its head at $0$, and the exit state carrying that symbol. There is a natural number $T$ at which this occurs such that, at every time $n<T$, the configuration has the original output, register $s$'s tape may have changed, and the heads of registers $s$ and $r$ are at positions $p$ and $q$ satisfying $-1\le p,q\le \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{bits}(\operatorname{length}(x)+1))$.
hypotheses_covered: Register $r$ contains the binary word for $i$
The head of register $r$ is at position $0$
